advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strip the trailing newline from `aws ssm get-parameter --output text` before piping into `gh secret set` (e.g. wrap with `printf %s "$(...)"` or `tr -d '\n'`) so mirrored token secrets are not stored with a trailing newline.
evidence: infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:104-107: `aws ssm get-parameter --region us-east-1 --with-decryption \   --name /rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key   --query Parameter.Value --output text \   | gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY --repo navapbc/rebar`
`aws ... --output text` emits the value followed by a trailing newline; `gh secret set NAME` reads the full stdin verbatim, so the stored secret gains a trailing `\n`.
RCA in the ticket/runbook: the section exists precisely to stop CI from running on wrong/stale credential values (2026-09-07 rotation).
advisory.finding: The documented sync commands pipe `aws ssm get-parameter ... --output text` into `gh secret set`; `--output text` appends a trailing newline, so the GitHub Actions secret is stored with a trailing `\n`. For token-style secrets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JIRA_API_TOKEN) a trailing newline can break authentication, reintroducing the broken-CI-credential class this runbook exists to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `printf %s "$(aws ssm get-parameter --region us-east-1 --with-decryption --name /rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key --query Parameter.Value --output text)" | gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY --repo navavpbc/rebar` (or pipe through `tr -d '\n'`) for each secret.

evidence: Diff adds `[\`ssm-secret-write-only.md\`](./ssm-secret-write-only.md#sync-mirrored-github-actions-secrets)` at mcp-client-pats.md lines 59 and 82 and provision-restore.md line 107 (confirmed via search_files)

ABSENCE: no assertion reads mcp-client-pats.md or provision-restore.md, and no assertion checks the `#sync-mirrored-github-actions-secrets` slug against the heading
advisory.finding: No test covers the cross-reference links added in the three sibling runbooks (mcp-client-pats.md x2, provision-restore.md) that point at `ssm-secret-write-only.md#sync-mirrored-github-actions-secrets`. The test asserts only that the target heading string exists in ssm-secret-write-only.md; it never asserts the three linking lines exist, nor that the anchor slug matches the heading. Renaming/reslugging the heading would silently break all three cross-references while the existing anchor-existence assertion continues to pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that reads mcp-client-pats.md and provision-restore.md, asserts the `./ssm-secret-write-only.md#sync-mirrored-github-actions-secrets` link is present in each, and derives the expected slug from the heading text so a heading rename fails the test.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the c57057f41 skip is acceptable (or ensure CI fetches enough history) so the parity regression guard is not silently skipped in shallow checkouts.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:273-274: `if historical_bat.returncode != 0:         pytest.skip("historical commit c57057f41 is absent from this checkout")`
tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:282-283: same skip for historical_test
A skipped test reports no failure; in a shallow checkout the guard produces its 'pass' outcome without running the assertion it exists to enforce.
blocking.finding: Converting the historical-commit lookups from `check=True` to `check=False` + `pytest.skip` means the parity regression guard silently no-ops in any checkout where commit c57057f41 is absent (e.g. shallow CI clones), so the test can pass without ever exercising the drift it was written to catch.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure test_sweep_extra_parity_would_have_caught_c57057f41 actually gates in CI (fetch the historical commit / assert its presence) rather than silently skipping on the shallow-clone default.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:273: `if historical_bat.returncode != 0:` then `pytest.skip("historical commit c57057f41 is absent from this checkout")`

Prior code used `check=True`, which raised CalledProcessError and FAILED loudly when the commit was absent; the diff changes both subprocess calls to `check=False` and converts the absence into a skip.
The test docstring names it the regression guard: `def test_sweep_extra_parity_would_have_caught_c57057f41()` — "The known historical workflow drift fails without an in-tree declaration."

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` checks out with `actions/checkout@...v7.0.0` (lines 50/251/325/413) and no `fetch-depth: 0` (search_files for fetch-depth in _build-and-test.yml returned no matches), so the shallow default clone will not contain `c57057f41` and this test will skip rather than run in CI.
blocking.finding: The 'would-have-caught-c57057f41' regression test now silently skips instead of failing when the historical commit is missing, and the CI runner's shallow checkout makes that skip the default path — disabling the guard in CI.
scenarios: A branch/main CI run using the shallow _build-and-test.yml checkout where c57057f41 is unreachable: the regression test reports skipped, providing no coverage.
A future change reintroduces the c57057f41-style undeclared sweep-extra drift; the guard designed to catch it is inert in CI.
blocking.suggested_fix: Either ensure the CI checkout for the unit-test lane fetches c57057f41 (or fetches it on demand within the test) so the skip path is never taken, or replace the live `git show` against a possibly-absent SHA with a checked-in fixture of the historical workflow so the regression assertion always runs.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the timestamp verification assert that all four expected mirror names are actually returned (e.g. count the matches / fail if any expected name is absent) rather than trusting empty jq output as success.
evidence: infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:135-136: `gh secret list --repo navapbc/rebar --json name,updatedAt   --jq '.[] | select(.name=="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" or ...)'`
The jq filter emits one line per matching secret; an absent secret yields no line, and the surrounding prose gives no instruction to assert all four names appear.

Litmus: the check emits nothing both when 'all four are present and current' is untrue-partial and when 'a name is simply missing' — its verdict cannot be distinguished from a producer that emitted nothing.
dropped.finding: The post-sync verification `gh secret list --repo navapbc/rebar --json name,updatedAt --jq '.[] | select(.name==...)'` produces empty output when a mirrored secret is absent (never created) — indistinguishable from 'the select matched nothing to flag'. The operator cannot tell 'checked and every mirror is present and fresh' apart from 'a mirror is missing', so the verification fails open.
